candidate.answerReason: The off-by-one clue gives possible ages 29, 31, 37, and 48. The low-guess condition leaves 37 and 48, and only 37 is prime.

methods.label: Combine the three age clues
methods.explanation:
Because the guesses are all different, two guesses can both be off by one only if one is a year below Norb's age and the other is a year above it. We therefore look for pairs of guesses that differ by \(2\). The only such pairs are
\[
(28,30),\quad(30,32),\quad(36,38),\quad(47,49).
\]
Their middle values give all possible ages: \(29,31,37,48\).

At least half of the ten guesses must be too low, so at least five guesses must be below his age. The fifth-smallest guess is \(36\), which means his age must exceed \(36\). This leaves \(37\) and \(48\).

Now \(48=6\cdot8\) is not prime. The number \(37\) is prime: it has no prime divisor \(2,3,\) or \(5\), and any composite number below \(49\) must have a prime divisor below \(7\).

At age \(37\), the five guesses \(24,28,30,32,36\) are too low, and \(36\) and \(38\) are each off by one. Thus Norb is \(37\) years old, choice C.
